:::

:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_size_factor`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Key in adata.obs for size factor information. Instead of using library size as a size factor,
the provided size factor column will be used as offset in the mean of the likelihood.
Assumed to be on linear scale.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_categorical_covariate`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Keys in adata.obs that correspond to categorical data. These covariates can be added in
addition to the batch covariate and are also treated as nuisance factors
(i.e., the model tries to minimize their effects on the latent space).
Thus, these should not be used for biologically-relevant factors that you do _not_ want to correct for.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_continuous_covariate`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Keys in adata.obs that correspond to continuous data. These covariates can be added in
addition to the batch covariate and are also treated as nuisance factors
(i.e., the model tries to minimize their effects on the latent space). Thus, these should not be
used for biologically-relevant factors that you do _not_ want to correct for.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--var_gene_names`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
.var column in the rna modality containing gene names. By default, use mod['rna'].var_names.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--var_protein_names`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}

### Model arguments

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--n_dimensions_latent_space`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Dimensionality of the latent space.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `20`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--gene_dispersion`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Set the behavior for the dispersion for negative binomial distributions:

  - gene: dispersion parameter of negative binomial is constant per gene across cells
  - gene-batch: dispersion can differ between different batches
  - gene-label: dispersion can differ between different labels
  - gene-cell:  dispersion can differ for every gene in every cell
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"gene"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"gene"`, `"gene-batch"`, `"gene-label"`, `"gene-cell"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--protein_dispersion`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Set the behavior for the dispersion for negative binomial distributions:

  - protein: dispersion parameter of negative binomial is constant per protein across cells
  - protein-batch: dispersion can differ between different batches
  - protein-label: dispersion can differ between different labels
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"protein"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"protein"`, `"protein-batch"`, `"protein-label"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--gene_likelihood`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Model used to generate the expression data from a count-based likelihood distribution.

- nb: Negative binomial distribution
- zinb: Zero-inflated negative binomial distribution
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"nb"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"nb"`, `"zinb"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--latent_distribution`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Set the latent distribution to use:

  - normal: Normal distribution
  - ln: Log-normal distribution (Normal( 0, 1) transformed by softmax)
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"normal"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"normal"`, `"ln"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--empirical_protein_background_prior`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Set the initialization of protein background prior empirically.
This option fits a GMM for each of 100 cells per batch and averages the distributions.
Note that even with this option set to True, this only initializes a parameter that is learned during inference.
If False, randomly initializes.
By default, sets this to True if greater than 10 proteins are used.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--override_missing_proteins`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
If True, will not treat proteins with all 0 expression in a particular batch as missing.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean_true`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/integrate/totalvi/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/integrate/totalvi);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/integrate/totalvi/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
